title: A Primer to (Cross-Cultural) Multi-Group Invariance Testing Possibilities in R
description: Methods article (Front. Psychol. 10:1507, published 18 July 2019) introducing the basic principle of measurement invariance testing, levels of invariance and differential item bias, and what to do when invariance is rejected, with R tutorials for multi-group confirmatory factor analysis (omnibus tests, individual restrictions and partial invariance, dMACS effect sizes), exploratory structural equation modelling, alignment, differential item functioning via ordinal/logistic regression, and EFA/PCA with Procrustes rotation, ending with an overall comparison of methods.

sections: Introduction; The Basic Principle of Measurement Invariance Testing; Levels of Measurement Invariance and Differential Item Bias (What to Do if Invariance Is Rejected?); Confirmatory Factor Analysis (running a multi-group CFA in R; omnibus test; individual restrictions and partial invariance; dMACS); Exploratory Structural Equation Modeling; Invariance Testing Using Alignment; Differential Item Functioning Using Ordinal Regression (Item Response Theory); Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) (Procrustes rotation with two groups); Overall Comparison of Methods; Summary
versions.licence: CC BY (version not stated in the copyright section)
limitations: Advanced: assumes factor analysis and R; it belongs after the reliability and validity material and basic regression.
Framed for cross-cultural group comparisons; whether it treats invariance across measurement occasions (longitudinal invariance) was not checked.
Frontiers' site-wide terms were not opened; import rests on the article-level CC BY statement.
